title: Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO Amid Affair and Espionage Allegations
summary:
Jensen Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has led it ever since, resigned as chief executive after reports of two extramarital affairs, one allegedly with a woman US officials believe is a Chinese intelligence asset. Finance chief Colette Kress becomes interim CEO, and long-serving director Harvey Jones becomes Nvidia's first board chair.

The exit matters because Nvidia, worth roughly **$3.8tn**, is the bellwether of the AI trade and was built around its founder.
context:
- Founder-led companies often command a premium for vision and continuity, so an abrupt exit raises key-person risk. Huang steered Nvidia's shift from gaming chips to the CUDA software ecosystem that underpins its AI dominance.

- The espionage angle matters because Nvidia sits at the centre of US export controls on advanced chips to China. The board says it has no reason to believe trade secrets were compromised and has launched an independent investigation.

- Third-quarter results on 17 November are the first test under Kress, a finance chief rather than a technologist. The board will consider internal and external candidates for the permanent role, leaving strategic direction uncertain for now.

title: Hot US Inflation Print Puts a Bigger Fed Hike on the Table
summary:
US consumer prices rose **0.4%** in October, with core inflation at **0.3%** for a third straight month, above forecasts. The reading met the threshold Fed Governor Christopher Waller had set for considering a half-point rise in December, and helped push the 10-year Treasury yield back above **5%**.

It matters because it suggests inflation is broadening beyond a temporary energy spike, narrowing the Fed's room to tighten gradually.
context:
- Economists cited energy costs linked to the Iran war, tariffs and housing as the main drivers, with shelter accounting for over 30% of October's increase. Services-led inflation tends to be stickier than fuel or goods prices.

- The 2025 government shutdown means no official 12-month rate was published, because October 2025 prices were never collected. That gap leaves the Fed leaning more heavily on monthly readings, which have been running hot.

- Markets now treat a December hike as near-certain, so the debate has shifted to its size. Higher Treasury yields feed straight into mortgage and corporate borrowing costs, tightening conditions beyond the Fed's own moves.

title: Anthropic Sets IPO Terms at Valuation of Up to $1.4tn
summary:
Anthropic, developer of the Claude AI models, set a price range of $70 to $78 a share for its Nasdaq listing under the ticker ANT, implying a valuation of up to roughly **$1.4tn**. It plans to sell 825 million shares, with trading expected to begin around 19 November.

The deal matters because it offers public investors a rare way to own a frontier AI developer directly, rather than through chipmakers and cloud providers.
context:
- Base proceeds of roughly **$58bn–$64bn** would rank among the largest listings in history, with reports describing it as potentially second only to SpaceX. The size tests how much fresh equity markets can absorb alongside heavy AI spending.

- A separate private placement of about $26bn from investors including Nvidia and Google shows suppliers financing their own customers. That circularity is a recurring concern for investors trying to gauge genuine AI demand.

- Reports say Anthropic is targeting an unusually large retail allocation of about 20%, while its founders retain control. Pricing in the same week as Nvidia's results makes it a broader referendum on AI valuations.
